title: Grateful Dead Live at Thelma Theater on 1969-12-12
source: Master Soundboard Reel > Reel to Reel > DAT > CDR

ai_review.summary: Soundboard recording that starts a bit harsh but settles into crystal‑clear Lovelights and a monster Alligator > Caution > Feedback sequence.
ai_review.review: The tape captures an early‑1970s Dead show where the mix is initially gritty, yet by the Lovelight suite the band shines with superb balance and a heavy Tom Constanten presence. Highlights include an extended, jazzy Alligator jam flowing into Caution and Feedback, plus standout moments from He Was A Friend of Mine, King Bee and the closing sequence. Recording quality improves dramatically halfway through, making the set highly enjoyable despite early roughness.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews are 5‑star, praising both performance and recording after the initial half; only one lukewarm review tempers the average, yielding a strong overall rating.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Early part described as 'grating' with heavy T.C. in the mix; later sections praised for clarity, balance and prominent keyboards. No major drop‑outs reported, but track segmentation (Alligator split) is a noted annoyance.

standout_songs: He Was A Friend of Mine
show_quality.setlist_flow: The set builds nicely, with the Lovelights providing a melodic high point before launching into an expansive Alligator‑Caution‑Feedback suite that keeps the momentum and showcases deep improvisation.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for his soaring guitar work ("Jerry Jam") and strong tone on King Bee; his playing drives the extended jams.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for "Phil Bombs" during the Alligator segment, delivering powerful bass foundations.
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten is heavy in the mix, highlighted as a key element of the performance and noted for his impending departure.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drum solo within Alligator receives enthusiastic mention; the energetic percussion section fuels the jam.
